Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the claim petition is not maintainable as per the provisions of Order XXXII Rule 1 to 5 that claimant has not filed claim petition but her elder sister has filed claim petition without filing an application for seeking leave to prosecute the case as guardian and next friend.

sentences.text: When this being the factual position regarding the health condition of the claimant affected due to accidental injuries, when the claimant is NC: 2023:KHC:26303 found to be not having sound mind, therefore, law enables to file suit ought to be filed through next friend/guardian.
The husband of the claimant died before the accident.
The claimant was a widow at the time of the accident.

Therefore, quite naturally, elder sister has filed a claim petition on behalf of the claimant in terms of the provisions of Order XXXII Rules 1 to 5 of CPC.
8.
For filing the suit/petition before the Court of Law/Tribunal, an express application need not be filed.
When a person has become disabled for various reasons, his right is not curtailed, but he can adjudicate his right through the next friend/guardian without filing application.

Therefore, if, in case the petitioner files suit/petition and during the pendency of the proceedings, he becomes unsound mind or disabled to prosecute for any other reason, then only an application can be filed seeking leave of the Court to prosecute the case by the said plaintiff/petitioner, for the reason that the plaintiff/petitioner is to be contested on behalf of him NC: 2023:KHC:26303 because of consequential development of becoming disabled to continue the proceedings.

Therefore, in the midst of the proceedings, if necessity arises for appointment of next friend/guardian, then an application can be filed convincing the court why there is necessity of appointment of next friend/guardian.
But when at initial stage, that means before filing suit/petition by the plaintiff/petitioner on behalf of disabled person an application under Order XXXII Rule 1 of CPC is optional.
Therefore, the petition filed by elder sister of the claimant is by exercising her right under Order XXXII Rule 1 of CPC.
Therefore, for the aforesaid reasons, filing of an application is not necessary in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Therefore, in this regard, I find no merit in the contention taken by the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: The Tribunal may invariably make it a point to require the evidence of the Doctor who treated the injured or who assessed the permanent disability.

13. We may now summarise the principles discussed above :
(i) All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
(ii) The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).
(iii) The doctor who treated an injured-claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:26303 the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv) The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession, occupation or job, age, education and other factors."

Therefore, the claim petition is not maintainable.
In the present case, it is the case of the claimant that the claimant had sustained grievous injuries to the head apart from fracture to the left first, third, fourth ribs.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The husband of the claimant died before the accident.
The claimant was a widow at the time of the accident.
Therefore, quite naturally, elder sister has filed a claim petition on behalf of the claimant in terms of the provisions of Order XXXII Rules 1 to 5 of CPC.
8.
For filing the suit/petition before the Court of Law/Tribunal, an express application need not be filed.
When a person has become disabled for various reasons, his right is not curtailed, but he can adjudicate his right through the next friend/guardian without filing application.
Therefore, if, in case the petitioner files suit/petition and during the pendency of the proceedings, he becomes unsound mind or disabled to prosecute for any other reason, then only an application can be filed seeking leave of the Court to prosecute the case by the said plaintiff/petitioner, for the reason that the plaintiff/petitioner is to be contested on behalf of him NC: 2023:KHC:26303 because of consequential development of becoming disabled to continue the proceedings.
Therefore, in the midst of the proceedings, if necessity arises for appointment of next friend/guardian, then an application can be filed convincing the court why there is necessity of appointment of next friend/guardian.
But when at initial stage, that means before filing suit/petition by the plaintiff/petitioner on behalf of disabled person an application under Order XXXII Rule 1 of CPC is optional.
Therefore, the petition filed by elder sister of the claimant is by exercising her right under Order XXXII Rule 1 of CPC.
Therefore, for the aforesaid reasons, filing of an application is not necessary in the facts and circumstances of the case.
The Tribunal held that as there was no acceptable evidence of income of the appellant, it should be assessed at Rs.900/- per month as the minimum wage was Rs.891 per month.
Therefore, with these conditions, the claimant becomes a disabled person not able to do her normal day to day functions.
Brain is a vital organ of the body and it controls all other organs of the body.
If 50% of disability is caused to the brain as per doctor's evidence, then certainly it affects the normal functions of a person.
The claimant was a Fisher Woman by profession as she was residing along the coastal side area.
